title: smart-search-router (LIVE on every Grep) hard-DENIES legitimate searches: any 3+-word pattern is classified 'semantic' and denied even when no semantic index exists, and two deny messages instruct the model to use Task(subagent_type="Explore") — the exact spawn the system elsewhere bans

evidence.quote: - \`Task(subagent_type="Explore", prompt="${pattern}")\` - agent exploration`;

hookSpecificOutput: {
      hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
      permissionDecision: 'deny',
      permissionDecisionReason: reason

causal_links: contradicts explore-to-scout's purpose (and today Explore is NOT blocked per D2b-01, so the bad suggestion is followable)
amplified by D2b-07 (PowerShell-per-daemon-query latency has no real timeout cap)
observe_how: Grep for an exact multi-word string (e.g. an error message "database is locked error") → classifyQuery returns 'semantic' → deny fires even on the no_index/daemon_unavailable/no-results branches (all four reason branches end in the same deny at L590-597). Structural queries are also denied with a hardcoded `--lang python` ast-grep suggestion regardless of project language (getAstGrepSuggestion L407-423). Each intercepted Grep also pays up to 6 sequential queryDaemonSync calls, each spawning a fresh PowerShell process on Windows (daemon-client.ts L570-585).
telemetry: This very review session: literal single-token Greps passed (allow path); multi-word patterns would have been denied. trackHookActivitySync routes counts to the TLDR daemon (not file-inspectable here)

title: smart-search-router ripgrepFallback builds a shell command by string-interpolating the model/content-influenced Grep pattern with only `"` and `$` escaped — cmd.exe metacharacters and bash backticks survive (injection), and the `2>/dev/null` redirect is invalid on cmd.exe so the fallback is broken on Windows anyway
causal_links: reachable from lookupSymbol/tldrSearch on every intercepted Grep whenever the daemon is indexing/unavailable
observe_how: A Grep pattern like `x" & calc & "` breaks out of the double quotes under cmd.exe; `%PATH%` expands inside quotes; under a bash shell backticks execute. The pattern is attacker-influenceable via prompt injection in repo content ('grep for <payload>'). Replace with spawnSync('rg', [pattern, dir, ...]) array args and drop the /dev/null redirect (use stdio:'pipe'). Note the same file's Windows daemon path interpolates the JSON query into a powershell -Command string (daemon-client.ts L570-585) with only single-quote doubling — fragile, same fix class.
telemetry: Fallback triggers whenever daemon response has indexing/unavailable status — i.e., on first Grep in any un-indexed project

title: smart-search-router (PreToolUse:Grep, registered-active) feeds the model's raw Grep `pattern` into an execSync cmd.exe shell-string (`rg "${escaped}"`), escaping only " and $ — the cmd.exe danger set (& | > < ^ %VAR%) passes through. Fires on EVERY Grep whenever the TLDR daemon is down. D5a saw this site and punted it as 'minor'.
causal_links: extends D5a triage (D5a labeled smart-search-router.ts:101 'minor, bounded by timeout+2>/dev/null' — re-rated here as live S1 injection on the Grep hot path)
telemetry: Stop the TLDR daemon (or run where it never started), issue a Grep whose pattern contains a cmd.exe metachar — e.g. pattern `foo & calc` or `x>poc.txt` — and observe the side-effect (file written / second command run). Count: on Windows `execSync` with no `shell` option uses %ComSpec% = cmd.exe; the escape regex at line 100 only handles " and $. Also note `2>/dev/null` at line 102 is a no-op on cmd.exe (creates a literal file named 'null').
observe_how: main() at line 447 reads `pattern = input.tool_input.pattern` (the model's Grep regex) and at line 455 calls extractTarget(pattern) UNCONDITIONALLY before any literal/early-return. extractTarget -> lookupSymbol(pattern) -> tldrSearch(`def ${pattern}`) / `class ${pattern}` / `${pattern} =`. tldrSearch tries the daemon first but falls through to ripgrepFallback(pattern) when the daemon is indexing/unavailable OR on ANY thrown error (catch, lines 89-92). ripgrepFallback builds `rg "${escaped}" "${projectDir}" --type py ... 2>/dev/null` with escaped = pattern.replace(/"/g,'\\"').replace(/\$/g,'\\$') and runs it through execSync (cmd.exe). cmd.exe treats & | > < ^ and %VAR% as live metacharacters — none are escaped — so a Grep pattern containing them executes/redirects. Same remediation class as D5a-01/02/03: drop the shell-string, use spawnSync('rg', [escaped, projectDir, '--type','py',...], {shell:false}).

evidence.quote: const pattern = input.tool_input.pattern;

// Try function first (most common)
  const funcResults = tldrSearch(`def ${pattern}`, projectDir);

title: Braintrust per-turn 'stop' finalizer is registered under SessionEnd, not Stop — every LLM span of the whole session is parented to the FINAL turn's span, and current_turn_span_id never resets between turns

evidence.quote:
def stop(input_data: dict) -> dict:
    """Handle Stop hook - creates LLM spans for model calls within the turn.

"command": "python C:/Users/david.hayes/.claude/hooks/braintrust_hooks.py stop",
            "timeout": 15000

"root_span_id": root_span_id,
            "span_parents": [turn_span_id],

set_session_value(session_id, "turn_last_line", line_num)
    set_session_value(session_id, "current_turn_span_id", "")

observe_how: The stop entry at settings.json:284 sits inside the "SessionEnd" block opened at line 264; grep of repo .claude/settings.json finds NO "Stop" event block, and the active-registration harvest lists no Stop event either. So during a live session each user_prompt_submit creates a fresh 'Turn N' span (braintrust_hooks.py:382-402) but the per-turn finalizer never runs: current_turn_span_id is only cleared at line 825, i.e. at SessionEnd. The single SessionEnd pass walks the ENTIRE transcript (turn_last_line starts at 0) and parents every create_llm_span event to the one turn_span_id read at line 575 — the LAST turn. Result: Turn 1..N-1 spans are empty shells with no end metrics, and the final turn span owns all LLM calls/tokens of the session. Any per-turn Braintrust analysis (braintrust-analyze, judge_session, the C.3 telemetry watch) reads misattributed traces. Gated on TRACE_TO_BRAINTRUST=true (braintrust_hooks.py:41); the corr-null 60.7% harvest metric indicates trace data is live. Fix: register `braintrust_hooks.py stop` under a Stop event block (its docstring's design), keep session_end at SessionEnd.
telemetry: harvest SUMMARY corr-null 60.7%; Braintrust: count LLM spans per turn span — expect ~all under the max turn id per session
causal_links: enables D10a-02 (stale span is never cleared, so the off-by-one read always finds it)
same per-prompt Python spawn frame as D6a-05
same wrong-span family as D2F-11 (hook-health-monitor attaches to session UUID)

title: package-install-guard is bypassed by any compound command (cd X && npm install evil) — all regexes are start-anchored, contradicting the rule claim that it 'intercepts all package install commands'

evidence.quote:
{ regex: /^pip\s+install\b/, ecosystem: 'pypi', skipTokens: 2 },
  { regex: /^uv\s+pip\s+install\b/, ecosystem: 'pypi', skipTokens: 3 },

function stripEnvPrefix(command: string): string {
  return command.replace(/^(\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^\s]*\s+)*/, '');
A PreToolUse:Bash hook (`package-install-guard`) intercepts all package install commands and runs a 4-layer security check before allowing execution.

observe_how: Every INSTALL_PATTERNS regex is anchored with ^ after stripEnvPrefix, so `cd .claude/hooks && npm install <pkg>`, `echo x; pip install <pkg>`, `bash -c "pip install <pkg>"`, or any pipeline/chained form falls through isPackageInstallCommand() -> outputContinue(). `cd <dir> && npm install` is one of the most common shapes Claude actually emits (this repo's own hook-dev workflow uses it), so the 4-layer supply-chain check is skipped in routine real usage while the rule doc asserts full coverage. Fix: split the command on shell separators (&&, ;, |, ||) and test each segment, as the typosquat/blocklist layers already operate per-package.
telemetry: Grep session transcripts for Bash commands matching /&&\s*(npm|pip|uv|pnpm|yarn)\s+(install|add|i)\b/ — each is an unguarded install.

title: plan-mode-approval-gate has a silent bypass: in --dangerously-skip-permissions sessions, transcript-resolution failure (missing/oversized transcript or no permissionMode entry) downgrades the intended 'deny' to 'ask', which the gate's own header documents is auto-allowed in bypass mode

evidence.quote:
* swallowed when the session was started with
 * `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: 187 ms after the gate's `ask`,
 * Claude Code's built-in PermissionRequest layer auto-allows

observe_how: When input.permission_mode reports 'plan' (the layered case the hook explicitly defends against), the underlying mode is recovered from the transcript. If that recovery returns null — transcript missing, size 0, size > 16MB (long sessions reach this), or no parseable non-plan permissionMode line — permissionMode becomes undefined and decideGate falls through to 'ask' (lines 115-121). In a bypass session 'ask' is auto-allowed per the hook's own empirical note, so the exact scenario the deny branch was built for silently re-opens for long-running bypass sessions. Secondary doc/code drift: comments claim an 8MB cap and 'backwards in 256KB chunks' (lines 184-186, 180) while the code uses a 16MB cap (line 142) and two full readFileSync passes (goal scan + mode scan) of the same transcript per ExitPlanMode. Fix: when rawPermissionMode === 'plan' and resolution returns null, deny (fail-closed) instead of ask.
telemetry: Check hook logs for 'Forcing plan-mode approval dialog' entries with rawPermissionMode='plan' and permissionMode=undefined in bypass sessions.

title: isRalphActive() has no TTL/staleness check — a stale .ralph/state.json with session.active=true permanently disables BOTH plan-mode-approval-gate and plan-to-ralph-enforcer for that project

evidence.quote: if (params.ralphActive) return { action: 'allow' };

observe_how: RalphSessionState carries last_activity ('epoch ms from Python') and ralph-delegation-enforcer even refreshes a heartbeat, but isRalphActive() never reads last_activity — only the boolean. If a Ralph run crashes or is killed without cleanup (this machine's MEMORY.md records exactly such a rogue multi-day Ralph loop), session.active stays true indefinitely and every plan-gate allow-branch fires forever: ExitPlanMode auto-allows with no dialog and post-plan code edits are never blocked. By contrast the sibling maestro-enforcer applies a 4h STATE_TTL — the asymmetry is the bug. SEED-07's doubled continuous-claude/continuous-claude/.ralph/ artifact shows stray .ralph dirs do occur in practice. Fix: treat active=true with last_activity older than ~4h as inactive.
telemetry: ls .ralph/state.json mtime vs session.active across projects; any active=true older than a day is a live gate bypass.
